title: "Comparing revisions and forecast errors"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette

  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Comparing revisions and forecast errors}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}

`readagau` compares vintages by semantic `observation_key`, not by row
position. This vignette builds a four-release sequence from the package's
small synthetic Crop Report workbook, then changes only release metadata,
status, and values. Every operation is therefore deterministic and offline;
the numbers below are demonstration values, not official estimates.

## Build an exact, semantic vintage sequence

The package readers supply the full observation schema (period, unit, basis,
geography, series identity, source sheet, and hash). We retain one Australian
Wheat production observation and make three forecasts followed by an estimate:

```{r build-vintages}
library(readagau)
library(knitr)

cache_dir <- tempfile("readagau-vintage-cache-", tmpdir = tempdir())
dir.create(cache_dir, recursive = TRUE)
state_path <- system.file(
  "fixtures", "workbooks", "crop-state.xlsx", package = "readagau"
)
stopifnot(nzchar(state_path), file.exists(state_path))

state <- read_crop_report(
  c(state = state_path),
  assets = "state",
  view = "canonical",
  cache_dir = cache_dir
)
base <- as.data.frame(state[
  state$geography == "Australia" &
    state$commodity == "Wheat" &
    tolower(state$concept) == "production" &
    state$period == "2025-26",
  , drop = FALSE
][1, , drop = FALSE])
stopifnot(nrow(base) == 1L)

release_ids <- c(
  "acr-2025-06-03-no-214", "acr-2025-09-02-no-215",
  "acr-2025-12-02-no-216", "acr-2026-03-03-no-217"
)
vintages <- base[rep(1L, 4L), , drop = FALSE]
vintages$release_id <- release_ids
vintages$release_date <- as.Date(c(
  "2025-06-03", "2025-09-02", "2025-12-02", "2026-03-03"
))
vintages$period_status <- c("forecast", "forecast", "forecast", "estimate")
vintages$status_source <- "synthetic vignette fixture"
vintages$value <- c(30560, 33765, 35585, 35985)
vintages$raw_value <- as.character(vintages$value)
vintages$sha256 <- vapply(seq_len(4L), function(i) {
  paste(rep(as.character(i), 64L), collapse = "")
}, "")

kable(data.frame(
  release_id = vintages$release_id,
  release_date = vintages$release_date,
  period_status = vintages$period_status,
  value = vintages$value,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
), row.names = FALSE)
```

The four rows share one semantic key. Their release IDs and dates order the
vintages; they do not become part of the observation identity. A duplicate key
within one release is rejected because it would make a revision ambiguous.

## Forecast revisions

`agau_forecast_revision()` compares adjacent forecast/projection values and also
reports when the final forecast becomes an estimate or historical value. It
provides both absolute and percentage revisions plus the issue-to-target
horizon in months:

```{r forecast-revisions}
forecast_revisions <- agau_forecast_revision(vintages)
forecast_display <- data.frame(
  old_release = forecast_revisions$old_release,
  new_release = forecast_revisions$new_release,
  old_value = forecast_revisions$old_value,
  new_value = forecast_revisions$new_value,
  absolute_revision = forecast_revisions$absolute_revision,
  percentage_revision = round(forecast_revisions$percentage_revision, 2),
  old_horizon_months = forecast_revisions$old_issue_to_target_horizon_months,
  new_horizon_months = forecast_revisions$new_issue_to_target_horizon_months,
  status_transition = forecast_revisions$status_transition,
  revision_number = forecast_revisions$revision_number,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
kable(forecast_display, row.names = FALSE)
```

The sign convention is `new_value - old_value`: a positive number means the
later vintage is larger. `revision_number` and `revision_count` are calculated
within each semantic observation, so adding another series does not change the
meaning of this result.

## First and latest revised realisations

To measure forecast error, append a later historical observation. With the
default `realisation = "first"`, each forecast is compared with the first later
estimate or historical value. `realisation = "latest_revised"` deliberately
selects the last such value and labels the comparison separately:

```{r forecast-errors}
latest_observation <- vintages[4L, , drop = FALSE]
latest_observation$release_id <- "acr-2026-06-02-no-218"
latest_observation$release_date <- as.Date("2026-06-02")
latest_observation$period_status <- "historical"
latest_observation$status_source <- "synthetic vignette fixture"
latest_observation$value <- 36010
latest_observation$raw_value <- "36010"
latest_observation$sha256 <- paste(rep("a", 64L), collapse = "")
vintages_with_realisation <- rbind(vintages, latest_observation)

first_error <- agau_forecast_error(
  vintages_with_realisation,
  realisation = "first"
)
latest_error <- agau_forecast_error(
  vintages_with_realisation,
  realisation = "latest_revised"
)

error_display <- rbind(
  data.frame(
    selection = first_error$realisation_selection,
    forecast_release = first_error$old_release,
    realisation_release = first_error$new_release,
    forecast_value = first_error$old_value,
    realised_value = first_error$new_value,
    forecast_error = first_error$forecast_error,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  ),
  data.frame(
    selection = latest_error$realisation_selection,
    forecast_release = latest_error$old_release,
    realisation_release = latest_error$new_release,
    forecast_value = latest_error$old_value,
    realised_value = latest_error$new_value,
    forecast_error = latest_error$forecast_error,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
)
kable(error_display, row.names = FALSE)
```

The error is also signed as `realised_value - forecast_value`; the percentage
error is retained in the returned column `percentage_error`. Neither selection
rewrites the source observations or silently replaces the first-realisation
concept.

Historical revisions are a separate operation. They compare two later
non-forecast statuses, so the appended estimate-to-historical change is
visible without being mislabelled as forecast error:

```{r history-revisions}
history_revisions <- agau_history_revision(vintages_with_realisation)
kable(data.frame(
  old_release = history_revisions$old_release,
  new_release = history_revisions$new_release,
  old_value = history_revisions$old_value,
  new_value = history_revisions$new_value,
  absolute_revision = history_revisions$absolute_revision,
  comparison = history_revisions$comparison,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
), row.names = FALSE)
```

For a package-facing workflow, `compare_agau_vintages()` dispatches these same
operations. Supplying parsed `data` keeps this example offline; supplying
named local assets is also supported, while a loader-based comparison uses
exact release IDs and the normal reader cache:

```{r compare-all}
all_comparisons <- compare_agau_vintages(
  product = "crop_report",
  data = vintages_with_realisation,
  releases = vintages_with_realisation$release_id,
  comparison = "all",
  cache_dir = cache_dir
)
kable(data.frame(
  comparison = names(all_comparisons),
  rows = vapply(all_comparisons, nrow, integer(1)),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
), row.names = FALSE)
```

## Structural breaks fail closed

A value change is not automatically a revision if the semantic basis changed.
For example, changing the unit from `kt` to `tonnes` creates a structural
break. `readagau` reports the changed metadata fields in a typed
`agau_validation_error` instead of joining incompatible observations:

```{r structural-break}
broken <- vintages_with_realisation
broken$unit[nrow(broken)] <- "tonnes"
broken <- readagau:::agau_rekey_data(broken)
break_condition <- tryCatch(
  agau_forecast_revision(broken),
  agau_validation_error = function(e) e
)

kable(data.frame(
  class = class(break_condition)[1L],
  message = conditionMessage(break_condition),
  changed_fields = paste(
    break_condition$structural_breaks$fields,
    collapse = "; "
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
), row.names = FALSE)
```

When this occurs in a real series, review the source metadata and create a
versioned concordance before comparing releases. Do not coerce units, markets,
geographies, or period bases merely to make a join succeed.
